name: priors
what_changed:
I added cross-season priors, built only from complete earlier seasons and keyed by player code and team code. build_priors.js writes priors_<season>.json, and the model reads it as d.priors. All edits in model.js are marked [exp_priors].
(1) Per-90 rates (PW). The player's previous-season totals of xG, xA, goals, assists, bonus, yellow and red cards, own goals, penalties missed and saved, saves (only when he was a GK) and DC (null before 2025-26, so it is skipped) are added as extra evidence with weight PW times last season's minutes: rate = (x_cur + PW*x_prev + posAvg*pm0) / (n90 + PW*n90_prev + pm0). The PRIOR_MIN pull toward the position average stays.
(2) Playing time (PK). Last season's share of matches played, share of appearances of 60 minutes or more, and minutes per appearance enter pPlay0, q60 and ePlay as PK pseudo-matches.
(3) Team strength (TR, TRP, NT). The team prior is last season's xG attack/defence ratio, or the promoted-side average from earlier seasons. When no such season exists, it falls back to the previous season's relegated sides. It is implemented but turned off (TR=TRP=0) because it was neutral on TRAIN.
In btRound the player code is now passed to pmPlayer. 2022-23 has no previous season, so its result equals the baseline exactly. Note: per-match xG in 2022-23 rounds 1-14 is 0, so the team stats skip rounds with no recorded xG.
TRAIN grid on 2023-24, about 45 replays, logs in logs/grid*.jsonl:
- PW: 0.1 gives 1.7639, 1 gives 1.7580, 3 gives 1.7557 (flat, slowly improving).
- PK: 1 gives 1.7538, 2 gives 1.7499, 3 gives 1.7503, 8 gives 1.7657 (too strong, pulls bias negative).
- Together, PK=2 and PW=1 give 1.7439, the best. PK 2-3 with PW 0.5-2 all fall between 1.7439 and 1.7456.
- Adding previous-season finishing (PFIN=1) is slightly worse (1.7464). Using the last 10 matches of last season for playing time instead of the whole season is worse (1.7477).
- Team priors at every TR/NT setting stay within ±0.001 of the best (better in rounds 4-10, worse later), so they are off.
- With the final config, 32 of 35 rounds in 2023-24 beat the baseline. By round range: 4-10 1.746 to 1.712, 11-20 1.756 to 1.739, 21-30 1.743 to 1.717, 31-38 1.823 to 1.810.
params: PW=1 (previous-season per-90 evidence counted at 1x its minutes), PK=2 (previous-season playing-time pattern as 2 pseudo-matches), PWD=0 (seasons older than last are ignored), PFIN=0, TR=0, TRP=0, NT=4. Production constants unchanged: PRIOR_MIN=450, K_FIN=3, N0=4, RECENT=6. PW and PK were chosen on TRAIN 2023-24 only.
risks:
- The validation gain is small and much smaller than the train gain: 1.6936 to 1.6897 (-0.004) against -0.022 on 2023-24. 2023-24 is the only train season with a previous season, so PW and PK are tuned on a single season. The validation gain could be partly noise.
- By position on 2024-25 (baseline then model): GKP 1.978 to 1.953, MID 1.578 to 1.562, FWD 2.092 to 2.095 (flat), DEF 1.678 to 1.693 (worse).
- The playing-time prior acts all season, not only early. Part of its train gain may come from the 6-match RECENT window being too short, rather than from cross-season information.
- Previous-season rates are not adjusted for a club change, a new role or a position change (saves are only used if the player was a GK).
- No train season has data from two seasons back, so older seasons get weight 0 (PWD=0). The 2024-25 JSON contains 2022-23 data, but it is not used for rates.
- Team priors were neutral, so they are disabled.
- PRIOR_MIN=300 looked slightly better on train together with the priors (1.7417), but I did not adopt it because it changes production behaviour, which the other experiment is tuning.
ship_notes:
How the live site gets the priors: publish data/priors.json, built by the build_priors.js logic from the last completed season (for 2025-26 that is 2024-25, and only ago=1 is needed). The file is about 90 KB for one season and has this shape: {players:{<player code>:[{ago,ty,m,xg,xa,g,a,bon,yc,rc,og,pmi,psv,sv,dc,n,np,n60,mp}]}, teams:{<team code>:[{ago,A,D,n}]}, promoted:{A,D,n,src}}. Fields can be trimmed to what the model uses. The site fetches it once, sets d.priors, and pmPlayer finds each player by p.code; the live data already has code in its cols.
The change only alters the rates (lamG, lamA, R.*) and the playing-time parameters (pPlay0, q60, ePlay), so the Monte Carlo ranges reflect it automatically, and the per-component breakdown is unchanged.
If the file is missing, or a player or team has no entry (new signings, promoted sides), the model falls back to exactly the current behaviour.
Once 2025-26 is complete, the DC rates in it will enter the priors automatically, because null values are skipped per stat.
